details: CONFIRMED by a probe. `_run` raises only on TimeoutExpired/OSError; a git that ran and died by a signal returns returncode -15
(subprocess raises nothing) and one that hit a fatal error returns 128. current_branch(strict=True) then does
`out if rc == 0 and out else None`, so both read as a detached HEAD, which is exactly what the front's 29 Oct decision says must
never happen ("a git call that failed or timed out must surface as 'git could not answer' ... and never be read as a detached HEAD").
`git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` exits 1 (and only 1) for a detached HEAD, so the distinction is exact. Given the concurrent SIGTERM item,
a killed git is a likely real cause of the 29 Oct failure, and this change would still print the misleading message for it.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: fake git `#!/bin/sh\nkill -TERM $$` on PATH, repo on wt/x:
rv.build_findings(repo, "a"*40, []) -> ERR nothing recorded: the worktree is not on a branch
git -C <non-repo> symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD -> exit 128; build_findings(<non-repo>) -> "the worktree is not on a branch"
failing_case: A fake git on PATH that does `kill -TERM $$` (what a stray SIGTERM to the gate's process group does to a git child, see the
open item a-gate-test-is-stopped-by-an-unknown-sigterm), repo on branch wt/x:
relay_git.git_strict(repo, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD") -> (-15, ""), no GitError;
rv.build_findings(repo, "a"*40, []) -> VerdictError "nothing recorded: the worktree is not on a branch".
Should be: "nothing recorded: git could not answer: git -C <repo> symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD, killed by signal 15".
Same for rc 128 (git ran and hit a fatal error): read as detached today.
fix_hint: In current_branch with strict: rc 0 and out -> branch; rc 1 -> None; any other rc -> raise GitError("git could not answer: <command>,
exit <rc>" or "killed by signal <n>" when rc < 0). Optionally make _run raise for rc < 0 in strict mode. Add pass cases 1-3 to
pass_cases: 1. fake git that kills itself with SIGTERM, repo on a branch -> build_findings raises VerdictError containing "git could not answer" and not "not on a branch".
2. fake git that exits 128 -> current_branch(dir, strict=True) raises GitError naming the command and "exit 128".
3. a real repo with a detached HEAD (git checkout --detach) -> current_branch(dir, strict=True) is None and build_findings says "the worktree is not on a branch" (symbolic-ref -q exits 1).
4. a real repo on wt/x -> current_branch(dir, strict=True) == "wt/x".
5. the existing timeout test (fake git sleeping past a 0.2 s limit) still gives "git could not answer".
reason: tests/test_verdict.py GitDiedOrFailed signal, fatal and detached-head tests pass; the first two fail without the fix.
findings.summary: a git killed by a signal (rc -15) or failing fatally (rc 128) is still reported as 'the worktree is not on a branch'

details: Question for the owner. What it is about: a gate test that failed once on 29 Oct in the inert probe (a second run of the whole test
suite in a temporary copy of the branch, run at the same time as the main run) and so stopped a landing. How it works: the test asks
git which branch the train is on; when git does not answer, relay read that as "not on a branch". Live example: the 29 Oct landing
of the queue-entries change stopped on exactly this. The front decided to fix the message, not the cause, so the next such failure
will be explained ("git could not answer ... killed by signal 15" once F1 is fixed) but will still stop the landing.
Options: (a) keep it so; the cause is chased by the open SIGTERM item, which is where the stray kills come from (recommended:
it is the measured shared state, a 20 s git timeout is not measured); (b) also add a follow-up item to make the probe tolerate one
transient git failure. PLAUSIBLE. Size: 0 (a note) or 30 agent minutes for (b).
